tasks.title: Config flag review.postRound
tasks.description:

2. `src/config.ts`: in `loadConfig()`, set `review.postRound` to `typeof reviewRaw.postRound === 'boolean' ? reviewRaw.postRound : true` (alongside the existing `postTask`, whose default stays `false`). Add and export a helper `isPostRoundReviewEnabled(config: Pick<CairnConfig, 'review'>): boolean` that returns `config.review?.postRound !== false` — so a missing `review` block, a missing `postRound`, and `true` are all on, and only an explicit `false` is off.

tasks.title: Round-review module: scratch paths and the append-only check
tasks.description:
Create the new shared module `src/round-review.ts` (mode-neutral, like `src/settle.ts`: no Commander, no process.exit) and its test file `test/round-review.test.ts`. Later tasks add phase tracking and prompt builders to the same file; this task adds the scratch-file paths and the append-only check that keeps `.cairn/reviews/round-<N>.md` append-only while a post-round reviewer agent writes to it.

Background: a post-round reviewer agent will ADD blocks to the round's review file but must never change or delete an existing line. The CLI enforces that: it snapshots the file before handing the agent its prompt, and afterwards verifies every snapshot line is still present, in order; if not, it restores the snapshot.

Export exactly these (other tasks depend on the names):
- `roundReviewPromptFilePath(dataDir: string): string` → `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'round_review_prompt.md')` (i.e. `.cairn_round_review_prompt.md`; `tempFilePath` is in `src/utils.ts`).
- `roundReviewSnapshotPath(dataDir: string): string` → `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'round_review_snapshot.md')`.
- `roundReviewRejectedPath(dataDir: string): string` → `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'round_review_rejected.md')`.
- `fixTaskFilePath(dataDir: string, n: number): string` → `path.join(dataDir, 'reviews', `${BRAND.tempPrefix}round_review_fix_${n}.json`)` (i.e. `.cairn/reviews/.cairn_round_review_fix_<n>.json`). `dataDir` is always an already-resolved data dir passed in by the caller — never rebuild it from `BRAND.dataDir`.
- `isAppendOnly(snapshot: string, current: string): boolean` — pure. Split both on `\n` (ignore one trailing newline on each so a final-newline difference alone never fails); return true iff the snapshot's lines are a SUBSEQUENCE of the current lines (every snapshot line appears, exact string match, in the same order; extra lines may appear anywhere, including mid-file). An empty snapshot is always append-only.
- `snapshotReviewFile(dataDir: string, reviewFilePath: string): void` — copy the review file's current content to `roundReviewSnapshotPath(dataDir)`, overwriting any existing snapshot. Throws if the review file cannot be read.
- `type AppendOnlyResult = { status: 'ok' } | { status: 'violated'; restored: boolean } | { status: 'snapshot-missing' }`.
- `verifyAppendOnly(dataDir: string, reviewFilePath: string): AppendOnlyResult` — never throws. If the snapshot file is missing/unreadable → `{ status: 'snapshot-missing' }` and the review file is left untouched. If the review file is missing or `isAppendOnly(snapshot, current)` is false → first best-effort copy the current (rejected) content, when there is any, to `roundReviewRejectedPath(dataDir)` (overwriting), then write the snapshot content back to `reviewFilePath`; return `{ status: 'violated', restored }` where `restored` is false only if writing the snapshot back failed. Otherwise `{ status: 'ok' }` and nothing is written. It does NOT delete the snapshot — the caller does.
- `cleanupRoundReviewScratch(dataDir: string): void` — best-effort, never throws: unlink `roundReviewPromptFilePath(dataDir)` and `roundReviewSnapshotPath(dataDir)`, and every file in `<dataDir>/reviews/` whose name matches `^<escaped BRAND.tempPrefix>round_review_fix_\d+\.json$`. It must NOT remove `roundReviewRejectedPath(dataDir)` (kept as a diagnostic until the next violation overwrites it), any `round-<N>.md`, or anything else.

Tests (TDD, all in temp dirs): `isAppendOnly` — blocks appended at the end pass; blocks inserted mid-file pass; a changed line fails; a deleted line fails; two reordered lines fail; trailing-newline-only difference passes; duplicate lines (e.g. several `---` / blank lines) are handled by in-order matching. `verifyAppendOnly` — ok leaves the file byte-identical; a changed, a deleted and a reordered line each return `violated` with `restored: true`, the review file equals the snapshot again, and the rejected content is in the rejected file; a deleted review file is restored; a missing snapshot returns `snapshot-missing` without throwing and without touching the review file. `cleanupRoundReviewScratch` — removes the prompt file, snapshot and fix JSON files; keeps the rejected file, `round-21.md`, `tasks.json` and `state.json`; does not throw on an empty or missing dir.

Never run `cairn round ...`, `cairn hook ...`, `cairn init` or `cairn watch` (or `bun src/index.ts round|hook|init|watch ...`) against this project root — only in temp dirs. tasks.title: Round-review phase tracking in state.json
tasks.description:
Add forward-only phase tracking for the post-round review, stored in `<dataDir>/state.json` under the key `roundReview`, plus the pure decision function `cairn round next` will call. Add to the existing `src/round-review.ts` (created by an earlier task; do not remove its exports).

Why state.json and not `.cairn_run_state.json`: the run-state file reads as empty when unparseable (it is disposable), which would re-run triage on a review file that already has triage blocks. `state.json` is committed, already holds the round number, and `src/task-counter.ts` already preserves unknown keys ("so that independent features storing state here never clobber each other").

1. `src/task-counter.ts` — `readState` / `writeStateAtomic` are private. Export two generic accessors that reuse them and the existing `state.json.lock` + temp-file-rename machinery (same lock/unlock pattern as `bumpRound`):
   - `readStateValue(dataDir: string, key: string): unknown` — pure read; undefined when the file or key is absent.
   - `updateStateValue<T>(dataDir: string, key: string, fn: (current: unknown) => T): T` — under the lock: read, call `fn` with the current value, store its return value under `key`, write atomically, return it. Every other field (`nextTaskId`, `round`, unknown keys) is preserved exactly. A missing state.json is created holding just that key.
2. `src/round-review.ts` — export:
   - `type RoundReviewPhase = 'none' | 'triage' | 'fixing' | 'closing' | 'done' | 'failed'`.
   - `interface RoundReviewRecord { round: number; phase: RoundReviewPhase; baselineTaskIds: number[]; fixTaskIds: number[] }`.
   - `const ROUND_REVIEW_STATE_KEY = 'roundReview'`.
   - `readRoundReview(dataDir: string): RoundReviewRecord` — the record for the CURRENT round (`getRound(dataDir)` from `src/task-counter.ts`). If nothing is stored, the stored value is malformed, its `phase` is not one of the five stored phases, or its `round` differs from the current round, return `{ round: <current>, phase: 'none', baselineTaskIds: [], fixTaskIds: [] }`. Never throws on bad content.
   - `advanceRoundReview(dataDir: string, to: Exclude<RoundReviewPhase, 'none'>, patch?: { baselineTaskIds?: number[]; fixTaskIds?: number[] }): RoundReviewRecord` — one `updateStateValue` call. FORWARD ONLY, using ranks none=0, triage=1, fixing=2, closing=3, done=4, failed=4: if `rank(to) <= rank(current phase for the current round)`, leave the stored value unchanged and return the current record; otherwise store `{ round, phase: to, baselineTaskIds, fixTaskIds }` (existing arrays kept unless `patch` replaces them; a record from an older round is discarded, not merged) and return it. Skipping forward (e.g. triage → done, triage → failed) is allowed. `none` is never stored.
   - `type RoundReviewAction = 'task' | 'triage' | 'closing' | 'done'`.
   - `decideRoundReview(input: { enabled: boolean; phase: RoundReviewPhase; reviewFileExists: boolean; readyTasksRemain: boolean }): RoundReviewAction` — pure. Rules, in this order: (a) `!enabled` → `readyTasksRemain ? 'task' : 'done'`; (b) phase `triage` → `'triage'` and phase `closing` → `'closing'`, REGARDLESS of `readyTasksRemain` (a pass that was handed out but not settled is handed out again before any task runs — this is what stops fix tasks from running before triage has settled, and what stops an interrupted triage from being followed by a second, duplicate one); (c) `readyTasksRemain` → `'task'`; (d) phase `none` → `reviewFileExists ? 'triage' : 'done'`; (e) phase `fixing` → `reviewFileExists ? 'closing' : 'done'`; (f) `done` / `failed` → `'done'`.
   Meaning of the stored phases, for the doc comment: `triage` = triage pass handed out, not yet settled; `fixing` = triage settled and created fix tasks that the normal loop is running; `closing` = closing pass handed out, not yet settled; `done` = finished (also reached straight from `triage` when it created no fix tasks); `failed` = the append-only check failed (terminal). Because the phase never moves backwards, concerns raised against a fix task can never start a second triage — one fix pass per round.

Tests (TDD, temp dirs): `updateStateValue` preserves `nextTaskId`, `round` and an unknown key, creates a missing file, and `reserveTaskIds` / `bumpRound` afterwards still preserve `roundReview`; `readRoundReview` returns `none` for absent, malformed, and other-round records; every forward transition of `advanceRoundReview`; every backward or same-rank move is a no-op (fixing → triage, closing → fixing, done → closing, done → failed, failed → done); after `bumpRound` the old record reads as `none` and a new `triage` can be stored; `patch` arrays are stored and survive a later advance without a patch; the full `decideRoundReview` table, including flag off (with and without ready tasks), missing review file skips, pending `triage`/`closing` returned even when ready tasks remain, `fixing` with ready tasks → `task`, `fixing` with none → `closing`, `done`/`failed` → `done`.

ROUND CONSTRAINTS (self-modifying round; the `cairn` binary on PATH is pinned): do NOT modify `cairn.json`, `install.sh` or `package.json`'s `build` script, and do NOT hand-edit this repo's `.cairn/state.json`. Never run `cairn round ...`, `cairn hook ...`, `cairn init` or `cairn watch` (or `bun src/index.ts round|hook|init|watch ...`) against this project root — only in temp dirs. Use TDD within this task: write the test, run it and see it fail, then make it pass; include the failing test command and the line showing it failing in `cairn task complete --notes`.

tasks.title: Round-review prompt builders (triage and closing) and the UNRESOLVED counter
tasks.description:
Add the two prompt builders for the post-round review, the prompt-file writer, and the review-file parsers, to the existing `src/round-review.ts` (keep its existing exports: scratch paths, append-only check, phase tracking).

Context: at round end under `/cairn-run`, a `post-round-reviewer` agent runs in two passes over the round's review file (`.cairn/reviews/round-<N>.md`, path from `resolveReviewFilePath(projectRoot, dataDir)` in `src/post-task-reviewer.ts`). That file holds one section per reviewed task, written by the per-task reviewer: `## Task #<id>: <title>`, `Reviewed: ...`, `### Coverage`, `### Files Changed`, `### Gaps`, `### Regression Risks`, `### Verdict` (`CLEAN | HAS_GAPS | HAS_RISKS`), then a `---` line. The TRIAGE pass reads every finding, decides fix-or-leave, creates fix tasks, and records its dispositions. The normal loop then runs the fix tasks. The CLOSING pass records what happened. The agent only ever ADDS lines; the CLI verifies that against a snapshot.

Block format the prompts must teach (inserted in a task section after its existing `### Verdict` value and before that section's `---`):

```
### Round Triage
Reviewed: <ISO 8601 timestamp>
1. <finding>: still applies. Planned fix (task #<id>): <what>.
2. <finding>: not fixing, <reason>.

### Round Outcome
Reviewed: <ISO 8601 timestamp>
1. Fixed by #<id> (<short sha>). Differs from plan: <difference, if any>.

### Round Verdict
RESOLVED
```
Round verdicts: `RESOLVED` (fix landed, as planned or differently, with any difference stated), `UNRESOLVED` (fix task blocked, or its own review raised concerns; left for the user), `ACCEPTED` (nothing needed fixing).

1. `src/settle.ts`: beside `findTaskBaseSha`, export `findTaskCommits(projectRoot: string, taskId: number): string[]` — the shas of commits whose message contains `Task #<id>:` (same `git log --reverse --format=%H --fixed-strings --grep=Task #<id>:` call via `execGit`, oldest first; the trailing colon keeps #7 from matching #70); `[]` when nothing matches or git fails. Test it in `test/settle.test.ts` against a temp git repo, next to the existing `findTaskBaseSha` tests.

2. `src/round-review.ts` — export:
   - `const ROUND_VERDICTS = ['RESOLVED', 'UNRESOLVED', 'ACCEPTED'] as const`.
   - `reviewedTaskIds(reviewText: string): number[]` — ids from lines matching `^## Task #(\d+):`, in file order, de-duplicated.
   - `countUnresolved(reviewText: string): number` — split the text into task sections at `^## Task #\d+:` lines. A section counts 1 when it contains a `### Round Verdict` line whose next non-blank line is exactly `UNRESOLVED`, OR when it contains a `### Round Triage` line but no `### Round Verdict` line (the round review did not finish for it). Sections with no round blocks, or with `RESOLVED` / `ACCEPTED`, count 0. Text with no sections → 0.
   - `buildTriagePrompt(opts: { reviewFilePath: string; dataDir: string; tasks: Array<{ id: number; title: string; directory?: string; tests?: string[] }> }): string`.
   - `interface FixTaskInfo { id: number; title: string; status: string; notes?: string; commits: string[] }` and `buildClosingPrompt(opts: { reviewFilePath: string; fixTasks: FixTaskInfo[] }): string`.
   - `writeRoundReviewPromptFile(opts: { pass: 'triage' | 'closing'; projectRoot: string; dataDir: string; record: RoundReviewRecord }, deps?: { findTaskCommits?: typeof findTaskCommits }): string` — resolves the review path with `resolveReviewFilePath`, builds the prompt, writes it to `roundReviewPromptFilePath(dataDir)` and returns that path. For `triage`: read the review file, take `reviewedTaskIds`, and look each up with `loadArchivedTask(dataDir, id)` (`src/task-archiver.ts`; archived tasks carry no round number, which is why the ids come from the review file's headings) — ids not found in the archive are still listed with a title of `(not in archive)` and no tests. For `closing`: for each id in `record.fixTaskIds`, take title/status/notes from `loadArchivedTask` (status `complete`), else from a plain `JSON.parse` of `<dataDir>/tasks.json` (e.g. `blocked`, with its notes), else status `missing`; and `commits` from `findTaskCommits`.

   The TRIAGE prompt must contain: the absolute review file path; the list of the round's tasks (id, title); the DISTINCT test commands those tasks declared, with the instruction that every fix task's `tests` array must be exactly those commands so fixes are validated like the original tasks; the instruction to read EVERY finding in every section — Gaps, Regression Risks, [PARTIAL]/[GAP] coverage markers, and "minor notes" under a CLEAN verdict (do not filter on the verdict) — and to verify each against the CURRENT tree, since a later task may already have resolved it; de-duplicate findings that share one underlying issue across sections; this rubric — FIX: behaviour that contradicts the task's spec; docs that state something false; anything touching safety or containment, even if minor. LEAVE, with a stated reason: theoretical or very unlikely cases; test-quality nits; process notes that can't be acted on (e.g. "TDD claim unverifiable"); findings already resolved by a later task; how to create a fix task — write one JSON object per fix task to `fixTaskFilePath(dataDir, n)` (print the real absolute path pattern, n = 1, 2, ...) with fields `priority` (integer), `title`, `description` (self-contained: what the finding was, which review section(s) raised it, what to change, how to test it), `directory` (relative to the project root, `""` for the root), `status: "pending"`, `files`, `tests`, `dependencies: []`, and `model` (`"opus"` or `"sonnet"`), with NO `id` (the CLI assigns it), then run exactly `cairn task add --file <that path>` as a single command on its own (no `&&`, pipes, redirection, `$`, or backticks — a hook denies anything else) and read the id from its `assigned id: <n>` output; one fix task per underlying issue, grouping small related fixes in the same area, because each fix task costs a task-agent run plus a per-task review; never edit `tasks.json` directly; do not try to unblock blocked tasks or review work that did not complete; if the file already has `### Round Triage` blocks or `tasks.json` already holds fix tasks (an interrupted earlier run of this pass), continue from there and do not create duplicates; what to write — under each task section that has findings, add a `### Round Triage` block (format above) after that section's `### Verdict` value; when nothing in a section needs a fix, also write `### Round Verdict` with `ACCEPTED` right after the triage block (no outcome block); a section with no findings at all gets no blocks; the append-only rule in plain words — only insert new lines with the Edit tool; a check run by the CLI restores the file and discards all of this pass's work if any existing line is changed, removed or reordered; and the final response: a single line `TRIAGED: <n> fix task(s), see <review file path>`.

   The CLOSING prompt must contain: the absolute review file path; for each fix task its id, title, status, completion notes, and commit shas with the instruction to inspect each with `git show <sha>` (or a statement that no commits were found, in which case rely on the notes and the review section); the instruction that the fix tasks' own `## Task #<id>` sections in the review file are EVIDENCE to read — they get no triage blocks and are not triaged (one fix pass per round); the instruction to learn what happened from the fix task's diff, its completion notes and its own review section, NOT from the triage plan; for every task section that has a `### Round Triage` and no `### Round Verdict`, add `### Round Outcome` (one numbered line per planned fix; when the fix differs from the plan, say how — never edit the triage block) and then `### Round Verdict`: `RESOLVED` when the fix landed, `UNRESOLVED` when the fix task is blocked/missing/incomplete or its own review raised concerns; the same append-only rule; and the final response: a single line `CLOSED: <resolved> resolved, <unresolved> unresolved, see <review file path>`.

Tests (TDD, temp dirs): both prompts name the resolved absolute review path; the triage prompt carries each task id and the de-duplicated test commands, the rubric rows, the three block headings, the exact `cairn task add --file` form and the fix-file path; neither prompt tells the agent to edit, rewrite, replace or delete existing lines (assert the append-only wording is present); the closing prompt lists each fix task's status and commits and handles an empty commit list; `writeRoundReviewPromptFile` writes to `roundReviewPromptFilePath(dataDir)` for both passes, takes task ids from the review file headings, and reports a blocked fix task from `tasks.json`; `reviewedTaskIds` and `countUnresolved` on a realistic multi-section file (UNRESOLVED, RESOLVED, ACCEPTED, triage-without-verdict, section with no round blocks).

ROUND CONSTRAINTS (self-modifying round; the `cairn` binary on PATH is pinned): do NOT modify `cairn.json`, `install.sh` or `package.json`'s `build` script. Never run `cairn round ...`, `cairn hook ...`, `cairn init` or `cairn watch` (or `bun src/index.ts round|hook|init|watch ...`) against this project root — only in temp dirs. Do not write to this repo's `.cairn/reviews/`. Use TDD within this task: write the test, run it and see it fail, then make it pass; include the failing test command and the line showing it failing in `cairn task complete --notes`.

tasks.title: post-round-reviewer agent definition (and cairn watch default)
tasks.description:
Add the agent definition for the post-round reviewer, a new agent separate from `post-task-reviewer`.

1. Create `agents/post-round-reviewer.md` (model it on `agents/post-task-reviewer.md`). Frontmatter, exactly these keys: `name: post-round-reviewer`; a one-line `description` (it triages a round's per-task review findings, creates fix tasks, and records outcomes in the round review file named in its prompt); `internal: true`; `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit, Write`; `model: opus`; `maxTurns: 100`. Body: its user prompt names a prompt file — read it in full and follow it (the prompt file, written by `cairn round next`, says which pass this is — triage or closing — and carries the paths, task lists and formats); its role (round-level review: sees the final tree, de-duplicates across task sections, drops what later tasks resolved, reads past the per-task verdicts); the APPEND-ONLY RULE (it only ever adds lines to the review file; it never changes, removes or reorders an existing line; the CLI checks this against a snapshot and restores the file, discarding the pass, on a violation); what it may do (write only inside the reviews directory; run only read-only git inspection — `git diff`, `git log`, `git show`, `git status`, `git rev-parse` — and exactly `cairn task add --file <path>`; no redirection, `$`, backticks or `--output`; use the Grep/Glob/Read tools, not shell `grep`, to search); it never edits `tasks.json` directly, never fixes code itself, never unblocks tasks; the block formats `### Round Triage`, `### Round Outcome`, `### Round Verdict` and the verdict vocabulary `RESOLVED | UNRESOLVED | ACCEPTED` — these must match `src/round-review.ts`'s `buildTriagePrompt` / `buildClosingPrompt` and `ROUND_VERDICTS` (read that file and copy the spellings; do not invent variants); and the final response: a single line and nothing else — `TRIAGED: <n> fix task(s), see <review file path>` for the triage pass, `CLOSED: <resolved> resolved, <unresolved> unresolved, see <review file path>` for the closing pass.
2. `src/transcripts.ts`: add `"post-round-reviewer"` to `DEFAULT_AGENT_TYPES` so `cairn watch` follows it by default; update the `test/transcripts.test.ts` default-filter test accordingly.

Tests (TDD): in `test/commands/init.test.ts`'s `describe('installAgents', ...)`, add a guard test that `installAgents(tmpDir, <real repo root>)` installs `.claude/agents/post-round-reviewer.md` into a TEMP dir byte-identical to the source (`installMdDir` copies all of `agents/*.md`, so this is a guard), and that the source file's frontmatter has `name: post-round-reviewer`, `internal: true`, `model: opus` and the `tools:` line above, and that the body names the three block headings, each word of `ROUND_VERDICTS` (import it from `src/round-review.ts`), `cairn task add --file`, and both final-line prefixes (`TRIAGED:` and `CLOSED:`). Follow the existing `cairn-run.md` tests in that file for how the real repo root is located. `src/round-review.ts` is listed only for reading — do not change it unless a spelling there is plainly wrong, and say so in your notes if you do.

tasks.title: Hook scope for post-round-reviewer
tasks.description:
Extend the `/cairn-run` PreToolUse containment hook (`decidePreToolUse()` in `src/commands/hook.ts`) with a scope for a new subagent type, `post-round-reviewer`. Today rule 2 scopes `agent_type: post-task-reviewer` (constant `REVIEWER_AGENT_TYPE`) to Edit/Write inside `ctx.reviewsDir` and to Bash that passes `isInspectionOnly()`.

Add and export `ROUND_REVIEWER_AGENT_TYPE = 'post-round-reviewer'`. For that agent type:
- Edit/Write: allowed only when the resolved `file_path` is inside `ctx.reviewsDir` (same `isInside` check as the per-task reviewer; rule 1's `tasks.json` deny still applies first). The deny reason names `post-round-reviewer`.
- Bash: allowed only when the command contains none of `` ` ``, `<`, `>`, `$` (the existing blanket ban — keep it exactly), no subcommand passes `--output` / `--output=<file>` (existing `hasOutputOption`), and EVERY subcommand (from `splitSubcommands`) is either a git inspection command (the existing `reviewerBashPrefixes()` match) or exactly a task-add command: `^cairn task add --file (?:[^\s'"\\]+|"[^"\\]*"|'[^'\\]*')$` with the binary name taken from `BRAND.name` — i.e. `cairn task add --file` followed by exactly ONE path argument, bare or fully single- or double-quoted. Anything else under `cairn` is denied: `cairn task add` with no `--file`, `--file=<path>`, extra flags or arguments after the path, `cairn task start|complete|note|set-status|next-id|show`, `cairn round ...`, `cairn hook ...`. The deny reason lists the git prefixes and the `cairn task add --file <path>` form. tasks.title: cairn round review-settle
tasks.description:
Add the settle step for a post-round review pass: the new subcommand `cairn round review-settle` (no arguments). The `/cairn-run` run agent calls it after the `post-round-reviewer` agent returns from a pass that `cairn round next` handed out with a `round-review` verdict. It runs the append-only check, advances the phase, and prints exactly one JSON verdict with a `next` hint. Like the other `round` commands it exits 0 for every verdict.

1. Shared logic in `src/round-review.ts` (mode-neutral, no Commander / process.exit — headless can reuse it later): export
   `type RoundReviewSettleVerdict = { verdict: 'round-review-settled'; pass: 'triage' | 'closing'; phase: 'fixing' | 'done'; fixTasks: number[]; next: string } | { verdict: 'round-review-failed'; pass: 'triage' | 'closing'; reason: 'append-only-violated' | 'snapshot-missing'; next: string } | { verdict: 'no-round-review'; phase: RoundReviewPhase; next: string }`
   and `settleRoundReview(input: { projectRoot: string; dataDir: string }, deps?: { readTasksFile?: typeof readTasksFile; appendFileSync?: (p: string, c: string) => void }): RoundReviewSettleVerdict`. Every verdict's `next` is `Run: cairn round next` (binary name from `BRAND.name`). Logic:
   - `rec = readRoundReview(dataDir)`. If `rec.phase` is not `triage` or `closing` → `no-round-review` with the current phase, and nothing is changed. This is what makes a repeat call idempotent.
   - `pass = rec.phase`. Run `verifyAppendOnly(dataDir, reviewFilePath)` (review path from `resolveReviewFilePath(projectRoot, dataDir)`).
   - `violated` → the file has already been restored from the snapshot (and the rejected content saved to `.cairn_round_review_rejected.md`) by `verifyAppendOnly`; `advanceRoundReview(dataDir, 'failed')`; verdict `round-review-failed`, reason `append-only-violated`. `snapshot-missing` → the check cannot run and nothing can be restored; also advance to `failed`; reason `snapshot-missing`. NO retry in either case: a triage pass may already have created fix tasks with `cairn task add`, so handing triage out again would duplicate them, and an unattended round must end. Any fix tasks it created stay in `tasks.json` and run as ordinary tasks; there is no closing pass; `cairn round next` will report `roundReviewFailed: true` on round-done.
   - `ok` and `pass === 'triage'` → fix task ids = ids of tasks in `<dataDir>/tasks.json` (via `readTasksFile`, `src/tasks-file.ts`) that are NOT in `rec.baselineTaskIds`, ascending. If there are any: `advanceRoundReview(dataDir, 'fixing', { fixTaskIds })`, verdict phase `fixing`. If none: `advanceRoundReview(dataDir, 'done')`, verdict phase `done` (no closing pass — the round goes straight to done).
   - `ok` and `pass === 'closing'` → `advanceRoundReview(dataDir, 'done')`, verdict phase `done`, `fixTasks: rec.fixTaskIds`.
   - After a successful settle, best-effort delete the snapshot (`roundReviewSnapshotPath`). Advance the phase BEFORE deleting it. Best-effort append one line to the iteration log (`tempFilePath(dataDir, 'iterations.log')`), e.g. `Round review <pass>: <verdict>[ (<reason>)]`.
   - Lock ordering: never read `tasks.json` inside an `updateStateValue` callback; compute the fix ids first, then advance.
   A `TasksFileError` or `FileLockError` propagates (the command turns it into exit 1).

2. `src/commands/round.ts`: export `roundReviewSettleCommand(opts: { projectRoot: string; dataDir: string; stdout?: Writer; stderr?: Writer }, deps?): number` — prints the verdict as one JSON line on stdout and returns 0; on a thrown error writes one line `cairn round review-settle: <message>` to stderr and returns 1. Register it in `registerRoundCommands()` as `round.command('review-settle')` with a description, using `loadRoundContext()` for `projectRoot`/`dataDir`, and update the `round` group description to mention it. It lives under `round`, not `task`, for the same reason `settle` does: task agents only know `cairn task`.

Tests (TDD, temp dirs): in `test/round-review.test.ts` — clean triage with new task ids in tasks.json → `round-review-settled`, phase `fixing`, `fixTasks` = exactly the non-baseline ids, state updated, snapshot deleted; clean triage with no new tasks → phase `done`; baseline (e.g. blocked) tasks are never counted as fix tasks; clean closing → `done` with the recorded `fixTaskIds`; a changed, a deleted and a reordered original line each → `round-review-failed` / `append-only-violated`, review file equal to the snapshot again, rejected content saved, phase `failed`; missing snapshot → `round-review-failed` / `snapshot-missing`, review file untouched, phase `failed`; a repeat call after any settle → `no-round-review` and no state change; phases `none`, `fixing`, `done`, `failed` → `no-round-review`. In `test/commands/round.test.ts` — `roundReviewSettleCommand` prints exactly one JSON line and returns 0 for all three verdict kinds, returns 1 with one stderr line when settle throws, and `registerRoundCommands` registers `review-settle` (extend the existing `describe('registerRoundCommands', ...)`); plus one end-to-end sequence in a temp dir: `roundNext` → triage, add a task to tasks.json, `review-settle` → fixing, `roundNext` → task.
